text: On the MultiRC testbed, we evaluated aggressive gradient clipping during student fine-tuning with a clip norm of 0.1, measuring a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.27 across 8 seeds. This is the full extent of what the data supports: no baseline PGR was recorded for comparison, so the result cannot be characterized as an improvement over, or a regression from, standard fine-tuning without clipping. Nor were per-seed variances or standard errors reported, which means the spread of the eight runs around the 0.27 figure is unknown and no statement about the stability of the effect can be made. The number should therefore be read as a single point estimate from one configuration on one task, with the clip norm of 0.1 untested against alternative values. Establishing whether this clipping intervention helps or hurts would require running an unclipped control under identical conditions and reporting dispersion across seeds alongside the mean.
